text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate observed for notifications pipeline -> Twilio 429s and SendGrid intermittent 502s. Affected: verification SMS and transactional emails. Alert group: notify-delivery-errors. Paging @tara (oncall).

tara: seeing spike on dashboards, verification success rate dropped from 99.8% to ~62% over last 10m. Customers complaining about delayed OTPs. Digging in now.

alex: grabbing logs. sample from gateway: `timestamp=1801234558 service=notify status=429 provider=twilio code=20429 attempts=3` and `timestamp=1801234560 service=notify status=502 provider=sendgrid`

josh: confirm both providers degraded? I can start failing over SMS to backup-sms-provider if we decide. Need a quick runbook step for toggling route.

lina: support queue is filling with "I didn't receive my code" tickets. Can we post a status update to customers?

alex: yes. quick triage: 1) Twilio is returning 429 (rate limiting) from multiple regions; retrying increases queue latency. 2) SendGrid 502s look like transient gateway errors. 3) Our retry loop is linear, causing bursts.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0032 | severity: high | owner: tara | runbook: notify-delivery-fallback https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/notify-delivery-fallback

tara: immediate mitigation plan: A) throttle internal dispatcher to reduce retries, B) enable provider fallback for SMS to backup-sms-provider, C) reduce email batch size and enable per-message retry jitter. Who can flip the failover flag? @josh or @alex?

josh: I can flip it. Will toggle `feature.notify.failover` to `backup-sms` and monitor. Command: ```
# flip provider route
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/feature-flags/notify.failover \ 
  -d '{"value":"backup-sms"}'
```

alex: while josh does that, I'll patch the dispatcher throttle: change `max_retries=3` -> `max_retries=2` and add exponential backoff base=1s -> 2s. Also patch circuit-breaker threshold to open on 50% error rate per minute for a provider.

josh: flip done. provider routes now: primary=twilio, fallback=backup-sms. logs: `route-change by=josh at=1801234590 status=ok`

tara: monitor metrics and SMS delivery latency. If backup-sms keeps up, we can keep it for next 30m then switch back. Alex, reduce email batch size now?

alex: reducing `email.batch_size` from 100 -> 20 and enabling jitter: `dispatch_jitter_ms=200-1200`. Deploying config change to prod: ```
kubectl set env deployment/notify DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE=20 DISPATCH_JITTER=200-1200
```

ops-bot: Deploy initiated by alex at 1801234622, rollout in progress.

lina: support announcement draft: "We're investigating delivery delays for verification codes and transactional emails. We're mitigating by routing SMS to a fallback provider and reducing email batch sizes. Some customers may still see delays up to ~15 minutes." Should we post?

mike: yes post now. Add: "No evidence of lost data; retries in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes or earlier."

tara: posting status update to status.redwood now.

ops-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-0032

alex: vendor outreach: pinged Twilio support with error samples (included request-ids). Twilio status link shows partial API throttling in region: https://status.twilio.com/incident/abc123 (observed 429 pattern). SentGrid support ticket opened with debug logs: https://support.sendgrid.com/tickets/SG-7890

josh: backup-sms is handling ~70% of traffic now, latency stabilized ~400ms. Twilio remains rate-limited; their support says "throttling due to upstream congestion, ETA unknown".

tara: customer impact assessment: affected customers are those in verification flows (signup and password reset) and transactional email senders with >500 daily sends. Estimated impacted sessions in last 15m: 1.1k verifications, 300 delayed emails. No evidence of permanent failures; most messages are queued.

lina: continuing to triage tickets, pushing canned reply: "We're routing to backup provider and reducing retries to avoid further delays. You may receive your code shortly. We will update as we have more info."

alex: safe rollback plan: If backup-sms shows higher error rate or costs spike >2x, revert feature flag to primary-only and enable queuing mode with user-facing delay message. Command to revert: ```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/feature-flags/notify.failover \ 
  -d '{"value":"primary"}'
```

josh: noting ticket to track cost delta and delivery rate. Also enabling metrics alert for backup provider error-rate >1% so we don't accidentally cause bigger issues.

tara: 30m status check scheduled at 1801236367. Handoff: I'll be primary owner for next 40m; alex will take over if I need to escalate. @mike please keep customer comms thread open.

ops-bot: Update: Deploy by alex completed at 1801234680, rollout 100%.

josh: metrics now: success rate for verifications improved to 95% after failover; email retries decreased errors by ~60%. Still monitoring for vendor recoveries.

lina: we pushed status note to critical customers via support portal. A couple enterprise accounts flagged as impacted — we should follow up directly after stabilization.

alex: vendor update: Twilio responded: "We've opened internal investigation; customers may see rate limiting while we rebalance. No ETA." SendGrid responded: "Transient gateway errors resolved in some regions; recommend retrying with exponential backoff."

tara: next steps: keep failover active, continue throttles, watch for cost spikes, prepare post-incident summary with timeline and customer impact. If vendors recover, coordinate gradual rollback and run a canary to primary providers for 5m.

mike: noted. I'll start incident summary doc and collect logs.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0032 | current status: mitigated (fallback enabled) | owner: tara | next update scheduled at 1801236367

josh: leaving a short note for oncall handover: `#handoff @alex for 1h`

alex: acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards until 1801238200 and prep rollback steps.
